raised.quote: verdicts: analysis.verdicts, search: deps.search, limit: probeLimit,
raised.claim: Probes and verification each get the full limit instead of sharing one search budget.
raised.why_it_breaks: With a limit of 120, 50 zero-candidate rows can make 100 probe searches and then 50 verification searches, for 150 calls against a configured cap of 120.

raised.claim: Setting `TRIAGE_PROBE_LIMIT=0` does not disable the verification gate.
raised.why_it_breaks: Production still supplies `search` at limit zero, so the gate runs, marks every attachment unverified without searching, and strips references that the documented opt-out should leave alone.

raised.claim: The triage cron sends requests through the raw Algolia client without consulting the persistent Algolia breaker.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the breaker is already open after repeated 429s, triage still starts its probes and verification against the same service during the cooldown. The startup invocation also supplies the raw client.

raised.claim: Triage enables live Algolia requests even when `UNTAPPD_LOOKUP_ENABLED` is false.
raised.why_it_breaks: An operator who turns off Untappd lookups can still trigger searches on startup during the triage window if pending rows and triage credentials exist; the cron wiring likewise does not consult the flag.

raised.claim: Duplicate verdicts for one beer can borrow each other's verification result.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the first verdict's query fails and a later verdict for the same beer succeeds, the later result overwrites the map entry and the planner publishes the first, unverified verdict under its first-wins rule. Reversing which query succeeds can suppress a valid first verdict.

raised.quote: verdicts: analysis.verdicts, search: deps.search, limit: probeLimit,
raised.claim: Verification spends its search budget on verdicts the planner will discard.
raised.why_it_breaks: With a one-search budget, an out-of-batch beer ID listed before a valid in-batch verdict can consume the only search. The planner later rejects the foreign ID, but the valid verdict has already lost its attachment.

raised.claim: Clearing references before routing validation converts invalid verdicts into persisted classifications.
raised.why_it_breaks: A matcher verdict that names both an existing issue and a new issue key should be rejected as contradictory. If verification fails first, both references are erased, the planner accepts the verdict as quiet, and the row leaves the untriaged pool.

raised.claim: Verification checks that a model-selected target exists, not that it is the orphan's beer.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the model proposes a query for an alcoholic sibling of a non-alcoholic orphan, finding that sibling passes the gate even when its ABV contradicts the shop row. The verifier has no orphan data or expected beer ID to catch the mismatch.

raised.claim: A successful search does not verify the claimed cause or distinguish it from an unchanged baseline.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a row whose original search already returned the right candidate, the model can repeat that same query while claiming a query-normalization bug. The gate approves the claim even though nothing about the query changed and the replay does not explain why matching failed.

raised.claim: The verifier misparses correctly formatted targets when the brewery contains a spaced dash.
raised.why_it_breaks: For brewery `North - South` and beer `Pils`, the requested target format produces `North - South — Pils`. The parser splits at the first hyphen and looks for brewery `North` and beer `South — Pils`, rejecting the real hit.

raised.quote: const number = await github.createIssue({ title: issue.title, body: issue.body, labels: issue.labels });
raised.claim: A new issue can still publish unverified examples and hypotheses in its original model-written body.
raised.why_it_breaks: If two verdicts reference one new issue and only one verifies, the remaining reference is enough to create the issue. Its title and body are unchanged, so they can still cite the rejected beer or make a claim that depended on it.

raised.claim: A temporary search failure is treated as a disproven cause and is not retried by triage.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a valid verification query times out, the job strips the attachment and records the row as reviewed. Once search recovers, the row is no longer eligible for triage unless its original candidate count crosses the zero/nonzero boundary.

raised.quote:
'Falsifiable causes: whenever you attach a verdict to an issue (issue_number or new_issue_key),',
    'you MUST also give `proposed_query` — the exact query you believe finds the beer — and',
    '`expected_target` as "<brewery> — <name>" you expect it to return. The query will be re-run and',
    'checked; if the target does not come back, the cause is discarded and only the classification is',
    'kept. Do not attach an issue when you cannot name a query that would find the beer; use',
    'not_on_untappd/wontfix, or matcher_bug with issue_number: null.
raised.claim: The search verification contract blocks actionable parser bugs that do not have an Untappd target.
raised.why_it_breaks: A shop adapter that incorrectly emits glassware as beer has a real parser bug, but there is no correct beer for a verification query to return. The new contract prevents that example from reaching a parser issue and even omits unattached `parser_bug` from the suggested alternatives.

raised.quote:
'Evidence fields for zero-candidate rows: `probe_brewery` is what Untappd returns for the BREWERY',
    'alone, `probe_name` for the NAME alone. "(no results)" means the probe RAN and Untappd holds',
    'nothing for it — strong evidence of absence; "(not run)" means no probe was made — no evidence.',
    'Use them instead of guessing: a brewery whose catalogue comes back but holds no such beer is',
    'not_on_untappd, not an alias gap; a beer found under a DIFFERENT brewery is a brewery-label',
    'problem; both empty means the beer is likely absent entirely.',
raised.claim: The prompt treats a top-three search sample as evidence about a brewery's complete catalogue.
raised.why_it_breaks: A beer can rank fourth on the brewery query and return nothing for the shop's alternate spelling. The payload omits the real hit, and the prompt tells the model to mark the beer `not_on_untappd`, which also blocks its metered fallback.

raised.claim: The newly included shop style bypasses the per-field prompt length cap.
raised.why_it_breaks: An oversized scraped style is copied through `...o` in full, so an anomalous style value can bloat the entire batch or push the request over the model's input limit despite the caps on the other scraped strings.

raised.claim: Unbounded model-generated text is accepted as a live third-party search query.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the model puts a long excerpt from issue data into `proposed_query`, the verifier sends that text to Algolia instead of rejecting it as an implausible beer query. The corresponding failure or downgrade log can also retain the full string.

raised.claim: The digest counts quietly recorded matcher and parser bugs as `wontfix`.
raised.why_it_breaks: A downgraded `matcher_bug` now enters `plan.quiet`, so it increments both `wontfix` and `unverified` even though the stored classification is not `wontfix`.

raised.claim: The quality-review metric counts causes as checked even when no verification search ran.
raised.why_it_breaks: Missing queries, malformed targets, and exhausted budget all produce entries in the verification map. A run with 40 missing queries can therefore report 40 causes checked and zero verification failures without making a single verification search.

raised.claim: The unverified digest count includes verdicts that will never be applied to the batch.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a one-row batch gets one valid verdict and ten out-of-batch verdicts whose checks fail, the digest can report one new row and ten unverified causes, even though none of those ten belongs to the batch.

raised.claim: A blank environment value silently selects zero rather than the default search budget.
raised.why_it_breaks: A deployment that defines `TRIAGE_PROBE_LIMIT=` coerces the empty string to zero instead of using 120. In the current wiring, that skips probes and silently suppresses all causal attachments.
